entry.name: mcs.2d.wave~
entry.description: 2d.wave~ is similar to wave~, but with an additional axis. A given ms range of an audio file will be divided into n rows. Y phase input will determine which row(s) will be used for playback. When the 2d.wave~ object is instantiated as mcs.2d.wave~ its outputs are combined into a single multichannel output but otherwise it functions identically to 2d.wave~.

arguments.name: buffer-name
arguments.description: Obligatory. Names theobject whose sample memory is used byfor its stored waveform. Note that if the underlying data in achanges, the signal output ofwill change, since it does not copy the sample data in a.always uses the first n channels of a multi-channel, where n is the number of theobject's output channels. The default number of channels, set by the third argument to theobject, is.

arguments.name: start and end-points
arguments.description: After thename argument, you can type in values for the start and end points of the waveform, as millisecond offsets from the beginning of aobject's sample memory. By default the start point is 0 and the end point is the end of the sample. If you want to set a non-zero start point but retain the sample end as the waveform end point, use only a single typed-in argument after thename. If ais connected to the start point (middle) inlet, the initial waveform start point argument is ignored. If ais connected to the end point (right) inlet, the initial waveform end point is ignored. The number of channels in the buffer~ file and the number of rows to be used may also be specified.

arguments.name: number-of-output-channels
arguments.description: Sets the number of output channels, which determines the number of outlets that theobject will have. The maximum number of channels is 8. The default is 1. If the audio file being played has more output channels than theobject, higher-numbered channels will not be played. If the audio file has fewer channels, the signals coming from the extra outlets ofwill be 0.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.description: Sets the inital number ofto divide the file into.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Double-clicking on theobject will open a window that displays the audio file loaded in the buffer associated with the object.

messages.name: float
messages.description: In 3rd or 4th inlets: Numbers can be used instead of signal objects to control the start and end points of the waveform, provided a signal is not connected to the inlet that receives the number.

messages.name: int
messages.description: In 3rd or 4th inlets: Numbers can be used instead of signal objects to control the start and end points of the waveform, provided a signal is not connected to the inlet that receives the number.

messages.name: rows
messages.digest: Set the number of sections to divide the file into
messages.description: The word, followed by an int, sets the number of rows a given range of an audio file will be divided into. The phase input signal value received in the 2nd inlet ofdetermines which row(s) are used for playback. The default value is 0.

messages.name: set
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, sets theused byfor its stored waveform. The symbol can optionally be followed by two values setting new waveform start and end points. If the values are not present, the default start and end points (the start and end of the sample) are used. If signal objects are connected to the start and/or end point inlets, the start and/or end point values are ignored.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: In left inlet: Input signal values progressing from 0 to 1 are used to scan a specified range of samples in aobject. The output of acan be used to controlas an oscillator, treating the range of samples in theas a repeating waveform. However, note that when changing the frequency of aconnected to the left inlet of, the perceived pitch of the signal coming out of 2d.wave~ may not correspond exactly to the frequency ofitself if the stored waveform contains multiple or partial repetitions of a waveform. You can invert theto play the waveform backwards.In 2nd inlet: Input signal values progressing from 0 to 1 are used to determine which of the row(s) specified by themessage will be used for playback. You can invert theto reverse the order in which rows are played.In 3rd inlet: The start of the waveform as a millisecond offset from the beginning of aobject's sample memory.In 4th inlet: The end of the waveform as a millisecond offset from the beginning of aobject's sample memory.
